meta.title: Murilo Gomes | Software Engineering Student
meta.description: Murilo Gomes's portfolio: his journey, projects, certifications and growth in software development.

hero.tagline: I learn something new every day and like to prove it in practice. Here's the path so far: every course, every project and every step of my growth.

journey.title: Journey
journey.statement: I wasn't born knowing how to code. I learned one course, one project and one mistake at a time, and I haven't stopped since.

items.title: Starting at SENAI
items.text: I enrolled in the Systems Analysis and Development technical program and started studying programming for real.

items.title: Certifications along the way
items.text: I collected certificates while I studied: LGPD (Brazil's data protection law), AWS Cloud Practitioner, Microsoft DP-900 and Web 3.0.

items.title: Capstone and graduation
items.text: I finished the program with a capstone project on facial recognition in Python, built to speed up patient check-in at medical insurance clinics.

items.title: A year of online courses
items.text: I focused on courses at Alura, Rocketseat and Hashtag Treinamentos. No classroom and no rush, but no stopping either.

items.title: Internship at Bozza
items.text: I started as an IT support intern, solving real problems for real people.

items.title: Arriving at FIAP
items.text: I started my bachelor's degree in Software Engineering. Graduation is expected in 2029.

items.title: Global Solution
items.text: I wrapped up a prototype that simulates quantum key exchange over a satellite link.

items.title: Presenting to Jovi Mobile
items.text: I presented REVI to Jovi Mobile, the company behind the challenge, at FIAP.

items.title: REVI at NEXT 2026
items.text: REVI, my team's project at FIAP, is being presented at NEXT 2026.

items.title: More events
items.text: I want to go to more tech events. The path keeps going and I'll keep updating it here.

experience.title: Experience
experience.highlightText: I learned SlideShow TV from its documentation and rolled it out at Bozza to display the company's internal announcements. HR used to hand out paper notices to reach the team; now the communication is digital, faster, cheaper and easy for everyone to access.

items.title: Onboarding
items.text: I built a form for HR and each department's managers, which helped new hires absorb information faster.

items.title: An organized IT room
items.text: I reorganized all of the equipment in the IT department.

items.title: Day to day
items.text: I handle support tickets, help users, maintain computers and reinstall Windows 10 and 11.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Five projects, each one taught me something different.

revi.name: REVI
revi.summary: A cognitive learning hub for Jovi's smartphone. It uses OCR and AI (Gemini) to turn photos from class into study material, like summaries, flashcards and practice tests. We presented it to Jovi Mobile at FIAP, and it was selected for NEXT 2026.
revi.part: Back-end and documentation for both the project and the system.
revi.learned: Working as a team on sprint deadlines, writing documentation other people can actually follow, and seeing a product get presented to a real company.
revi.imageAlt: REVI presentation video, with the team, the app screens (flash cards, mind map, tasks, ranking and folders) and the QR code to try it.

gs.name: QKD Satellite Security Prototype
gs.summary: An Arduino prototype that simulates quantum key distribution (QKD) over a satellite link. LEDs stand in for photons, the system measures their states, calculates the error rate (QBER) and rejects the key when it goes above 11%.
gs.part: The hardware prototype: Arduino Uno, C++, an I2C LCD, a buzzer, LEDs and a potentiometer, plus a simulation in Wokwi.
gs.learned: The challenge was taking a very abstract topic and making it visible and interactive. I learned how to split work across a team and how to explain a complex subject visually.
gs.imageAlt: Wokwi simulation of the Arduino prototype: green, yellow and red LEDs, potentiometer, buzzer, button and LCD display. Press play to watch the simulation.

gogames.name: GoGames
gogames.summary: An online store in Python that simulates a purchase, with a shopping cart and shipping costs calculated by state.
gogames.part: The whole project, with a focus on writing clean code.
gogames.learned: Single-responsibility functions, no repeated code, and data kept separate from logic. Code that anyone can read and change.
gogames.imageAlt: Terminal showing the GoGames store menu: about the store, checkout and exit, with the purchase total.

tcc.name: Facial recognition for patients
tcc.summary: A Python system that uses facial recognition to speed up patient check-in at medical insurance clinics.
tcc.part: The development in Python with face-recognition, OpenCV, Pillow and NumPy, and the MySQL database.
tcc.learned: It was my first time working with computer vision and my first big project carried from start to finish. I learned to start from a real problem, slow check-ins, and turn it into something that works.
tcc.imageAlt: Window of the facial recognition system identifying a patient, with a green frame around the face and the data on screen: name, age, partially hidden CPF, last appointment, scheduling and procedure.

portfolio.name: This portfolio
portfolio.summary: The site you're looking at: a scroll-driven page that tells my professional and academic story, in Portuguese and English, with light and dark themes and animations.
portfolio.part: Content, structure, choice of visual references and review of every step, with AI as a development aid.
portfolio.learned: Organizing a whole page into components, handling two languages and two themes, and testing on many screen sizes. I also learned to ask clearly, review what was generated and fix what didn't turn out right.
portfolio.imageAlt: Home page of this portfolio, with the name Murilo Gomes in large type, resume and journey buttons, and the numbers for certifications, projects and years of study.
